Under the current **NHS Breast Screening Programme**, **routine screening is not offered at age 30**. Here's what you need to know:

### 🔹 Standard NHS Screening
- **Age range**: Women aged **50 to 70** in England (Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland also start at 50, though some areas are piloting an earlier start at 47).
- **Interval**: Automatically invited for a mammogram **every 3 years**.
- **Age 30**: You will **not** be invited for routine NHS breast screening at this age.

### 🔹 If You're at Higher Risk
If you have a **strong family history** of breast or ovarian cancer, a known **genetic mutation** (e.g., BRCA1/2, PALB2, CHEK2), or other significant risk factors, you may be eligible for **enhanced screening**:
- You can ask your GP for a referral to a **clinical genetics service** or **high-risk breast clinic**.
- High-risk screening typically starts around **age 40** (sometimes 35–38 depending on individual risk), and may include **annual mammograms and/or breast MRI**.
- Starting at 30 is only considered in very specific, high-risk genetic cases under specialist guidance.

### 🔹 What to Do at Age 30
- Practice **breast awareness** (know what's normal for you and report changes promptly).
- See your GP if you notice: a new lump, skin dimpling, nipple changes, unexplained discharge, or persistent pain.
- GPs may offer a **clinical breast examination** or refer you for an **ultrasound** if symptoms arise (mammography is less effective in younger, denser breast tissue).

### 📚 Official Sources
- NHS England: [nhs.uk/breast-screening](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/breast-screening/)
- NHS Breast Screening Programme guidelines: [nhsbspprogramme.org.uk](https://www.nhsbspprogramme.org.uk/)
- High-risk screening: [nhs.uk/conditions/breast-cancer/risk-factors/](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/breast-cancer/risk-factors/)

Under the NHS Breast Screening Programme, the standard screening interval is **every 3 years**.

**At age 72:**
- You are **no longer automatically invited** for routine screening (automatic invitations typically cover ages 50–70, depending on your birth date and region).
- However, you **can continue to be screened** by **self-referring**. You can contact your local breast screening unit or GP to request a mammogram. If accepted, you will continue to be invited every 3 years.
- Self-referral is available across England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland, though administrative processes may vary slightly by region.

**Important notes:**
- If you have symptoms (e.g., a lump, nipple changes, or pain), you should see your GP promptly rather than waiting for screening.
- If you have a strong family history or known genetic risk, your GP may recommend more frequent or earlier screening outside the standard programme.
- The NHS is gradually expanding the automatic invitation age range in some areas, but as of 2024/2025, age 72 still requires self-referral in most regions.

For the most accurate local information, visit [NHS.uk/breast-screening](https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/breast-screening/) or contact your local breast screening service directly. Always discuss personal risk factors with your GP.
